newsitem.title: USA: Sanfilippo & Son says high costs hurt 1996 results.
newsitem.headline: Sanfilippo & Son says high costs hurt 1996 results.

text.p: John B. Sanfilippo & Son Inc said high raw material costs contributed to the nut company reporting a lower gross profit margin and net loss for 1996.
"With 1996 behind us we look forward to a solid future and a profitable 1997," said chief executive Jasper Sanfilippo.

The processor and seller of nuts under such brand names as Evon's and Fisher reported a net loss for 1996 of $3 million on sales of $294.4 million, versus a 1995 profit of $5.8 million on sales of $277.7 million.

"As a result of the negative impact of the high costs of some raw materials that could not be recovered in pricing, the company's gross margin declined from 16.9 percent in 1995 to 13.3 percent in 1996," the company said.

Fourth-quarter margin was 14.7 percent, compared to 14.3 percent in the year-ago period. Fourth-quarter profits were $1.5 million on sales of $106 million, versus a year-ago profit of $2.7 million on sales of $104.7 million.
Higher sales on the year were credited by the company mainly to the first full year of Fisher Nut sales. The line was acquired by Sanfilippo in November 1995.
The company also said its selling and administrative expenses rose on the year to 12.0 percent of net sales from 10.9 percent in 1995.
Interest expense on the year increased to 3.1 percent of net sales from 2.8 percent in the prior year "as a result of higher working capital requirements," the company said.
